All constructs are consistent with standard AUR packaging practices. Nothing in the top-level scope would trigger unsafe behavior when sourcing the PKGBUILD for metadata extraction.

<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package build configuration. It declares standard fields such as package name, description, version, dependencies, source location, and checksums. The source points to a Git repository at `https://github.com/Mayware/userspawn`, which aligns with the package's stated upstream. The `sha256sums = SKIP` entry is expected for Git sources in AUR packages, especially `-git` variants, because the content is inherently mutable and checksums cannot be pinned. This practice, while reducing reproducibility, is normal and not inherently malicious.

No executable code or scripts are present in this file. It does not perform any system operations, network requests, or file modifications. It solely serves as declarative metadata for the PKGBUILD and AUR tooling. There is no evidence of obfuscation, unauthorized data exfiltration, or suspicious commands. All listed dependencies (cmake, git, ninja, dbus) are relevant to building and running a CMake-based systemd/dbus service on Arch Linux.

The package provides and conflicts with `userspawn`, indicating it’s an alternative implementation or development version of a base package, which is common in AUR. No red flags such as unexpected binary blobs, external download URLs, or encoded payloads are present.
</details>
